notesStmt.note: This is one of several similar documents, printed copies of the poem to which Whitman made the same series of minor, hand-written alterations and annotations, probably for the purpose of presenting them as souvenirs. In the notes of his visit to Whitman on 31 October 1889, Horace Traubel mentions that he received such "slip copies" of this and another poem (See With Walt Whitman in Camden, vol).proof is likely from 1889, the year of the poem's publication.
A proof sheet of "Bravo, Paris Exposition!" with corrections in Whitman's hand.

lg.head: BRAVO, PARIS EXHIBITION Exposition!
lg.l: Add to your show, dear before you close it, France,

With all the rest, visible, concrete, temple, towers, goods, ma-
chinesmachines and ores,

Our sentiment wafted from many million heart-throbs, ethereal
but solid,

(We grand-sons and great-grand-sons do not forget your grand-
sires,)

From fifty Nations and nebulous Nations, compacted, sent
over-sea to-day,
America's applause, love. memories and good-will.
